fix: f32::clamp panics when min > max, and apply_restored_window_options runs before options.validate() (open_window_inner L372-373 and open_window_with_inner L422-423). App-author options with minimum > maximum therefore panic instead of returning WindowOptionsError::MinimumExceedsMaximum when a saved window matches. Replace the clamp calls with non-panicking bounds: `saved_size.width.max(minimum.width).min(maximum.map_or(f32::MAX, |size| size.width))` and the same for height. Validation still runs afterwards and returns the error.

The retained root builder closure (L486-498) clones restoration_scope on every root rebuild. RestorationScope::clone allocates a Vec<RestorationKey> (each key owns a String) for any non-empty path. Hoist the value once before the closure (`let restoration_scope = restoration_scope.map(Rc::new);`) and change BuildContext::new to take the shared handle (Option<Rc<RestorationScope>>, or &RestorationScope), so each rebuild only bumps an Rc count. Keep the initial clone at L454 consistent with the same change.

RestorationManager::windows() (restoration.rs L699) clones the whole snapshot Vec<RestoredWindow>, including every restoration_id and kind String, and then discards all but one. Add a pub(crate) lookup such as `fn window(&self, restoration_id: &str) -> Option<RestoredWindow>` on RestorationManager that clones only the matching entry, and call it here as `manager.window(metadata.id.as_key().as_str())`.

Each active restoration_id String is cloned into a HashSet<String> only to answer membership queries. Avoid the clones and the extra Vec: `let mut windows = manager.windows(); let active_ids: HashSet<&str> = active_windows.iter().map(|window| window.restoration_id.as_str()).collect(); windows.retain(|window| !active_ids.contains(window.restoration_id.as_str())); windows.extend(active_windows);` in the retain_unopened branch. The borrow ends before extend moves active_windows, which is why the clone was a borrow workaround.
